title: PUBG Mobile WOW Halloweeks: Brainrot and Creator Maps
summary: Learn how the limited Halloweeks theme fits World of Wonder and what map creators should check.
intro: World of Wonder has allowed PUBG Mobile players to try user-created experiences beyond standard battle-royale matches. Version 4.6's public announcement mentioned a temporary Halloweeks transformation for Brainrot-related gameplay. This guide focuses on finding legitimate creations, understanding seasonal availability and designing maps that continue to work when decorations change.

sections.heading: Limited events versus permanent creative tools
paragraphs: A Halloweeks-themed promotion is not proof that every World of Wonder map receives the same features. Check an individual creation's live description and the event selector. Seasonal assets or interactions may disappear or move when the activity ends. Avoid following old video instructions that depend on an unavailable item. A useful map should communicate its objective even if its seasonal look is removed.

sections.heading: What makes a map worth replaying
paragraphs: Clear spawn points, understandable win conditions, balanced routes and consistent device behavior matter more than the number of decorations. If you build a simple obstacle course, show players where it starts and what signals completion. If you build a team challenge, test that both teams receive comparable access. Invite someone unfamiliar with the map to try it; their questions often reveal problems the creator missed.

sections.heading: Brainrot themes should serve the gameplay
paragraphs: A humorous or chaotic theme can draw attention, but it should support a coherent challenge. Choose a limited number of mechanics that interact well rather than stacking every moving object and audio effect available. Test the experience on an ordinary phone, not only a powerful device. Heavy effects may create frame-time spikes when several players enter the same area, and a laggy map tends to lose returning visitors.

sections.heading: 4.7 brings a different creator preview
paragraphs: The third 4.7 beta announcement describes an improved Smart Assistant and Smart Editor that can generate complex scenes from conversation. That could help with a rough layout, but a generated scene still requires collision checking, performance testing and objective design. No beta notice proves that a written prompt automatically creates a publishable balanced game. Treat creator AI as an assistant, not a replacement for playtesting.

sections.heading: Publish safely and accurately
paragraphs: Use original descriptions of your map's objective, recommended players and length. Do not promise free UC or official premium cosmetics unless the publisher actually authorizes the reward. Avoid copying another creator's work or inserting unnecessary outside contact details. Keep a version note when you fix a map, so players know why it changed after an event or game update.

sections.heading: Make a map that survives the seasonal change
paragraphs: Try playing your map while mentally removing the Halloween decorations. Can a new visitor still locate the start, understand the goal and recognize success or failure? If the answer depends entirely on a special object available only during Halloweeks, plan a replacement before the event ends. Test each device on an ordinary mobile phone and ask a newcomer to describe the instructions back to you. Clear rules and responsive fixes give a custom mode lasting value, while a trending visual theme without functional gameplay usually loses its appeal quickly.
